messages:
Alex: Heads up — planning to rename the routing header from `X-Route` -> `x-rd-route` and add a new policy enum `narrowcast`. Targeting a phased rollout next week, want SDK & console impact thoughts.

Priya: @Alex what's the compatibility window? will servers accept both for a while? :thinking_face:

Alex: Yes — server will accept both headers for 30 days. Console will start surfacing `narrowcast` as a separate policy which will change quota attribution in some dashboards.

Jordan: For SDKs, I can add a fallback so older clients keep working. Question: do we want SDKs to expose a typed enum or keep it as a raw string? Typed enum is nicer ergonomically but risks breaking callers.

Maya: Typed enum would be a breaking change. We should do a soft-typing approach: runtime enum helpers + opt-in strict validation (env var) so existing code doesn't break.

Lee: Go client currently does strict header validation in the transport layer — that will break customers unless we relax it.

Alex: Proposal: (1) server accepts both headers for 30d; (2) SDKs ship soft validation that logs WARN and prefers `x-rd-route` when present; (3) console adds telemetry tag `route_policy.v2` to allow filtering; (4) rollout flag in console to enable narrowcast per-tenant for testing.

Priya: Can we add a console-facing rollout toggle per customer? that'd really help partners test without impacting global metrics.

Jordan: I'll implement WARN logs and an env var `RD_ROUTE_STRICT=true` to opt into strict enum checking. Default remains permissive.

Maya: QA checklist — add e2e that verifies quota attribution flips when `narrowcast` is used, and a regression test for header precedence (if both headers present). Also coordinate with billing for sampling changes.

SRE Bot: Deploy window scheduled Thu 03:00 UTC. Canary 5% us-west, then 20% after 30m if no errors.

Lee: Go PR relaxing validation is draft; unblocks after API review. Also found a subtle bug: when both headers present, we currently pick the legacy header. I think we should prefer `x-rd-route` (v2).

Alex: Good catch. We should prefer v2 value. Please file a bug and assign to the PR.

Lee: Filed #1234 and assigned to self. Patch coming.

Jordan: Release notes draft: python 1.4.3 — adds fallback header handling + WARN logs; ts 2.0.1 — adds enum helper + opt-in strict mode; go 0.9.7 — relaxes strict transport validation (soft mode). Make sure wording explicitly reassures customers: no forced break during 30d window.

Priya: Docs: add migration snippet and recommended QA steps. Also add a console tile called `Routing policy drift` to show percent legacy vs v2 header usage over time.

Maya: Suggest adding telemetry fields: `route_policy.source` (sdk|manual|gateway), `route_policy.version` (v1|v2), and `route_policy.migration_stage` (canary|gradual|ga). That will make dashboard queries simpler.

Alex: Agreed. We'll add those fields to the telemetry payload. Make sure sdks include `route_policy.version` in trace headers for sampling.

Lee: Small regression: when both headers present, Go picks legacy. Patch switches precedence. Tests added.

SRE Bot: Canary rollout started — 5% traffic routed to canary. Monitoring alerts: none at T+20m.

Jordan: Migration guide snippet for devs (to include in docs):
```
# python example
headers = {"x-rd-route": "narrowcast", "X-Route": "broad"}
# SDKs will prefer x-rd-route when present; set RD_ROUTE_STRICT=true to enforce enum checks
```

Maya: QA: add a test that simulates both headers and asserts SDK chooses v2 value + that console attribution lines up with request samples.

Priya: Timeline recap: announce docs today, SDK PRs posted today, canary tomorrow, full GA after 30 days acceptance window. Add a postmortem checklist in case of data drift.

Alex: Thanks all. I'll send the docs + migration mail and update the release plan. :rocket:
